rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: Any landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice delivered with Notice to Quit / non-renewal; copy filed with Office of Housing Stability
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, including on eviction, lease non-renewal, or post-foreclosure purchase. The requirements cannot be waived by lease or other agreement.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exempt if the residence is in a hospital, skilled nursing or health facility, or in a non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility.

rules.penalty: Enforced by Inspectional Services Department: 1st offense warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: City of Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7)
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
rules.conflict_note: Citation is taken from the FAQ's penalty table, 'Sec. 10-11.7', and may refer to the penalty schedule rather than the codified ordinance section.
